sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: product incident liaison: accept the structured morning rotation

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the issue ledger and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The support rota review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I am comfortable answering routine support questions in a shared channel.
Do ordinary questions unsettle you?
No, when the evidence is already attached.
Someone new shadowed me in the product desk this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the launch weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For the billing outage, I listed observed symptoms, possible causes, and unanswered questions before I accepted ownership at the 09:30 huddle.
What happened after you used that list?
We assigned checks without claiming a cause too early.
I can host a short morning triage after I have sorted reports into confirmed and open points.
What makes that useful?
Everyone can see what is known and what still needs checking.
I archived last cycle's notes on the support rota and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My focus is clearest before lunch and drops after a long afternoon of ticket review.
Does timing change how you handle ambiguity?
Yes, I need more structure later in the day.
A vendor call about the issue ledger ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the product desk checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the launch weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the support rota records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
A Monday-to-Friday 10:00 office hour has been proposed, with a shared evidence worksheet completed before each discussion.
Could you take that rotation?
Yes, that timing and worksheet give me a sound basis to respond.
I sketched next week's plan for the launch weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the issue ledger updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
When the worksheet is incomplete, the support lead can keep the item open until the next morning rather than demand a live answer.
Does that help?
Yes, it keeps uncertainty visible instead of turning it into a guess.
I compared two options for the support rota tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the product desk handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The support lead has offered me the weekday 10:00 escalation office hour with the shared worksheet. Is that a role I should take on?

I did a standard pass over the support rota records this morning.
The proposed office hour is moved to 15:30 and callers will be asked to summarize from memory without the worksheet.
Would that be the same arrangement?
No, it removes both the timing and evidence conditions that make it workable.
